chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly a systematic eschatological/cosmological teaching (three ‘days’ as three great temporal-cosmic phases; two ‘deaths’ as two distinct modes of loss/separation). The only clear frame is the opening dialogue apparatus. A late Christianising moral-causal tag appears at the end of ¶15 (‘blasphemed … the Holy Spirit’), appended to an otherwise cosmological description of the second death.

paragraphs.core_text: There exist three great mighty days in all; and also two great and bitter deaths.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame and audience-address/application voice: “Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples: Happen you know, my beloved ones,”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with explicit Kephalaia dialogue attribution (‘apostle … disciples’) and direct address (‘my beloved ones’), marking a later compiling frame; the underlying numbered teaching topic (three days/two deaths) is the core schematic.
Q&A apparatus (‘When … heard, they say to him’) characteristic of the editorial dialogue frame; functions as a prompt rather than impersonal exposition.
Minimal speech-attribution seam (‘He speaks to them.’), purely editorial dialogue mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: The first day is our father, the Man. From the time when the First Man went down to the abyss of Darkness and drowned in it; and the Living Spirit was sent, who went and bore him up. After the Man had ascended, the Father of Life and the Great Spirit set things in order, and the worlds above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological narration of the First Man descent/rescue and ordering of worlds; all referents remain within the Manichaean cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, the glorious Ambassador came and dwelt in the ship of the day. He displayed his glorious image, and he purified the light out of all things. He walked in the heights of the heavens. Till the time when the world will be dissolved, all things destroyed, the great fire released, and the Last Statue ascends. These three deeds were begun on this first day, when they sent the First Man with his five sons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic, process-oriented eschatological mechanics (purification, dissolution, great fire, Last Statue) with named cosmic beings; no citation or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.103⟩ In contrast, [the first death] is the Darkness that mixed with the five sons of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Definition stays entirely within cosmic substances/beings (Darkness mixing with First Man’s five sons), matching the old ‘what it is’ explanatory register.

paragraphs.core_text: The second day is the time when the fathers of light, who were victorious in the struggle, will sit on their thrones in the new aeon and dwell on the new earth. And they reign in the new aeon till the Father unveils his image above them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological timetable stated as cosmic chronology (new aeon/new earth, Father unveiling image), not institutional exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The {length of the sojourn} in the new aeon equals the measure of the first day spent in affliction. They will reign like this and rejoice in the new aeon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Temporal-measure correspondence (duration equals measure) in impersonal doctrinal voice; no frame or moral application.

paragraphs.core_text: The great third day [is the time] when the Father will unveil over them his image ... ... and he raises them up [ ... ] and he receives them into his hidden treasury ... and he gives [ ... ] his soul. He can pour out upon them ... his ambrosia and his sweet perfume, which takes away all affliction that they have seen with their eyes. [ ... ] fullness and a joy eternal! When his grace would sate them, he gives to them his [ ... ] and they are made anew in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core eschatological ‘unveiling’ and reintegration into the hidden treasury; imagery (ambrosia/perfume) functions as intra-system transformation language, not NT citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, he can summon them once more in peace and silence, and perfect their stature in same measure as his first aeons. And he sets each power in its aeon, in its dwelling-place. They will dwell in the new aeon in their aeons!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/order-setting motif (‘each power in its aeon’) is classic systematic cosmological arrangement; no external referencing.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, when they dwell in their aeons, they will become rich beyond measure, for ever, beyond time. From then on they will not count that season amongst them; nor the number of the days, nor the hours, generation after generation, for ever and ever. The Father will not be hidden from them, from this time on. Rather, he has accomplished (his) unveiling to them [ ... ] he being revealed to them for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal description of timelessness after unveiling; remains cosmological (‘Father … unveiling’) rather than ecclesial/pastoral.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the three great days, [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative numeration formula (‘given number … in the reckoning’) fits the chapter’s systematic temporal classification.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, the two deaths that I have proclaimed to you are these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural transition within the teaching sequence; no institutional vocabulary or external authority citation.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.104⟩ The first death is from the time when the light fell to the Darkness, and was mixed in with the rulers of Darkness; until the time when the light will become pure, and be separated from the Darkness in that great fire. The remainder left behind there can build and add to that Last Statue.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic mixing/separation mechanics (Light/Darkness; rulers; great fire; Last Statue) in impersonal doctrinal voice—strong core substrate texture.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the second death is the death in which the souls of sinful men shall die; when [they will] be stripped of the shining light that illuminates the world. And also they are separated from the living air, from which they receive [living] breath; and they are deprived of this living soul, which [ ... ] in the world; and they are separated and swept away from this Last Statue [ ... ... ] and bound on [ ... ... ] the female will become [ ... ] their torture and their affliction; for their deeds [ ... ] those three places;
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the Christianising moral-causal tag: “because they have blasphemed and despised the Holy Spirit since [ev]ery generation of the world.” This shifts from cosmological mechanics to confessional blame-language anchored in Christian pneumatology.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The first part remains intra-system: stripping from Light/air/breath/soul, separation from the Last Statue, binding and torment—cosmic process description. The final ‘Holy Spirit’ clause is a later Christian overlay expression appended as moral explanation.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the two deaths. The first death is temporal; [but] the second death is eternal. It is the sec[ond deat]h!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Doctrinal closure in a definitional/register-summary style (temporal vs eternal) without dialogue frame or institutional application.
